prerequisites: Competencies related to the design, organization, and architecture of computers, as well as computer networks.
Competencies in software design and development.
Reading and comprehension skills for technical documentation in English.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the design guidelines in microcontroller-based systems.
Design hardware based on module integration.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to embedded and ubiquitous systems
Practical case: Development of firmware for a real-time system module and its integration with modules developed by other peers to implement a real embedded system.
teaching_methods: Classroom practices (module integration and programming for simple embedded systems)
Individual laboratory practices (module-based embedded system design, mandatory delivery exercises)
Group laboratory practices (related to coordinated project, presentation required)

assessment_methods.method: Theory evaluation (classroom activities and/or Virtual Campus)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, the final grade must be 5 points or higher out of 10. In the ordinary call, it is essential to attend at least 80% of active laboratory practical classes. If this attendance requirement is met, the final grade is calculated as 0.3 * NTeo + 0.7 * (0.5 * NPracEjer + 0.5 * NPracProy). If the attendance requirement is not met, the final grade is 0.3 * NTeo. In the extraordinary call, theory is evaluated by an individual written exam (NExTeo) and practicals by NExPrac (same as ordinary if >= 5.0, else 0). If NExTeo is >= 5.0, the final grade is Maximum(NExTeo; 0.6 * NExTeo + 0.4 * NExPrac); otherwise, the final grade is NExTeo. For differentiated evaluation, students take a final theory exam (NDifTeo), a final practical exam (NDifPrac), and submit all laboratory practice exercises (NDifEjerPrac). To take the theory exam, NDifEjerPrac must be >= 5.0. To take the practical exam, NDifTeo must be >= 5.0. The final grade is 0.5 * NDifTeo + 0.5 * NDifPrac if NDifEjerPrac >= 5.0, otherwise it is NDifEjerPrac. New evaluations are conducted in each call, without considering previous exam grades.
